title: Know your phone: buy well, get online, keep it healthy

say: Know your phone: buy well, get online, and keep it healthy.
This is the video for Module 1 of Smartphone and Digital Awareness: getting to know your smartphone.
A small button phone makes calls and sends text messages. A smartphone does that too, but it is really a small computer. It goes on the internet, runs programs called apps, and takes good photos.

say: Storage is the space for apps, photos, videos and voice notes. Small storage fills up fast with WhatsApp photos.

panel.heading: The four numbers that matter
items: Storage, for example 64 GB: room for photos
RAM, for example 4 GB: runs apps smoothly
Battery, for example 5,000 mAh
Android version: newer stays safe longer

say: RAM is the phone's working memory. Low RAM makes a phone slow.

panel.heading: The four numbers that matter
items: Storage, for example 64 GB: room for photos
RAM, for example 4 GB: runs apps smoothly
Battery, for example 5,000 mAh
Android version: newer stays safe longer

say: The battery number, in mAh, tells you how much charge it holds. Bigger usually means longer use.

panel.heading: The four numbers that matter
items: Storage, for example 64 GB: room for photos
RAM, for example 4 GB: runs apps smoothly
Battery, for example 5,000 mAh
Android version: newer stays safe longer

say: And the Android version. Newer versions get security updates for longer.
For example, Hauwa in Kano compares two phones at about the same price. Phone A has double the storage, double the RAM and 25% more battery, so she chooses it, and she asks for a written receipt.

say: Mobile data comes through your SIM card, and you pay for it with data bundles. Swipe down twice from the top and tap the Mobile data tile to switch it on.

panel.heading: Mobile data or Wi-Fi?
right: Comes from a router or hotspot

say: Wi-Fi comes from a router, a MiFi, or another phone's hotspot. Long press the Wi-Fi tile, tap the network name, type the password exactly, and tap Connect.
On free Wi-Fi shared with strangers, do not open your bank app. Use your own data for anything with money.

say: Most phone damage comes from heat, poor charging, drops and water. Charge on a table, never under a pillow or in a bag, and never with wet hands. When power returns after an outage, unplug the charger and wait for the power to settle.

cards.d: On a hard, open surface. Never under a pillow, on a bed or with wet hands. Use a good charger.
Back lifting or very hot? Stop using and charging it. Never press or pierce it. Take it for repair.
Switch it off. Do not charge it. Remove case and SIM tray. Air dry, no hairdryer or sun.

say: If the back of your phone is lifting, or it gets very hot and smells strange, stop using and charging it at once. Never press or pierce a swollen battery. Take it to a qualified repairer.

say: If the phone gets wet, switch it off and do not charge it. Remove the case and SIM tray, and let it dry in open air for a long time. No hairdryer, oven or sun.

say: Do these five checks once a week. Charger and cable undamaged. Screen protector not cracked. Charging port clean and dry, with no pin pushed in.
At least 15% of storage free, so the phone stays fast. And restart the phone once a week, which fixes many small problems.

panel.heading: Weekly phone care check
items: Charger and cable undamaged
Screen protector not cracked
Port clean and dry
At least 15% storage free
Phone restarted this week

say: To remember. Compare the four numbers before you buy. Set a 6-digit screen lock that is not your birthday.
Dial star, hash, zero, six, hash to see your IMEI, the 15-digit number for your phone, and write it down.
Check the internet in order, and charge on a hard, open surface.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Compare storage, RAM, battery and Android
Set a 6-digit screen lock PIN
Dial *#06# and record your IMEI
Check: Airplane, signal, data, balance
Charge on a hard, open surface
